config.title: Build role based access middleware

intro.title: Build role based access middleware
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a role-based access middleware function for a Node.js application. This middleware will check a user's role from a request and allow or deny access to specific routes. You'll learn how to use Express middleware, conditional logic, and HTTP status codes to enforce access control. The main technologies involved are Node.js, Express, and JavaScript functions. By the end, you'll have a reusable middleware that can protect routes based on user roles.
intro.usecase: Role-based access control (RBAC) middleware is a fundamental pattern in any multi-user application where permissions differ by user type. For example, in a SaaS dashboard, an admin might see user management panels and billing settings, while a regular user only sees their own profile and usage data. This middleware ensures that API endpoints or UI routes are protected, preventing unauthorized access to sensitive operations like deleting records or viewing financial reports. As a Node.js developer, you'll implement this to secure backend services for e-commerce platforms, internal admin tools, or collaborative apps, where defining clear access boundaries is critical for security and user experience.

objectives: Implement middleware functions that intercept HTTP requests in a Node.js application
Construct role-based access control logic using conditional statements and role arrays
Configure Express middleware to validate user roles before allowing access to protected routes
Apply role checking middleware to specific routes while leaving public routes unrestricted
Initialize a role verification system that extracts user information from request objects
Integrate role-based middleware with existing authentication systems to create layered security
Manipulate HTTP response objects to send appropriate status codes when access is denied

steps.title: Define user roles and permissions
steps.instruction: Create a roles object that maps role names to arrays of permissions. Define three roles: 'admin' with permissions ['read', 'write', 'delete'], 'user' with permissions ['read', 'write'], and 'guest' with permissions ['read'].
steps.hint: Create a JavaScript object where keys are role names and values are arrays of permission strings.
steps.expectedOutcome: A roles object is created with three roles (admin, user, guest) and their corresponding permission arrays.
successCriteria: The roles object exists with correct role names and permission arrays as specified.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started defining roles, but check that all three roles (admin, user, guest) are included with their correct permission arrays.
steps.feedbackWrong: The roles object is missing or doesn't match the required structure. Make sure to create an object with three roles and their permission arrays as specified.

steps.hint: Define an array with user objects like { id: 1, name: 'Alice', role: 'admin' } and { id: 2, name: 'Bob', role: 'user' }.
steps.expectedOutcome: An array named 'users' is created with at least two user objects containing id, name, and role properties.
successCriteria: The 'users' array exists and contains objects with id, name, and role properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your array is named 'users' and contains at least two objects with id, name, and role properties.
steps.feedbackWrong: The mock user data wasn't created correctly. Create an array named 'users' with objects containing id, name, and role properties.

steps.title: Define the role checking function
steps.instruction: Create a function named 'checkPermission' that takes two parameters: 'userRole' and 'requiredPermission', and returns true if the user role has that permission, false otherwise.
steps.hint: You can use the roles and permissions object you defined earlier to look up the permissions array for the given userRole, then check if requiredPermission is included in that array.
steps.expectedOutcome: A function named 'checkPermission' is created that correctly validates permissions based on user roles.
successCriteria: The 'checkPermission' function exists, accepts two parameters, and returns a boolean value based on permission validation.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created a function, but make sure it's named 'checkPermission' and properly checks if the required permission exists in the user role's permissions.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function isn't quite right. Create a function named 'checkPermission' that takes userRole and requiredPermission parameters and returns true/false based on permission validation.

steps.title: Add role extraction logic to middleware
steps.instruction: Inside your middleware function, add logic to extract the user ID from the request URL query parameters and find the corresponding user from your mock data array.

steps.expectedOutcome: The middleware function will be able to extract a user ID from the URL and locate the corresponding user object from the mock data.
successCriteria: The middleware function contains logic to parse the request URL, extract a userId query parameter, and find the matching user from the users array.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using the url module to parse the request URL and extract the userId query parameter, then using Array.find() to locate the matching user from the users array.
steps.feedbackWrong: The middleware function doesn't yet extract user information from the request. Remember to parse the URL to get query parameters and find the matching user from your mock data.
